title: I just got my keys. How do I let out the unit?
videoTitle: 4 Things to Know to Let Out Your Unit | Vlog 006
excerpt: After the keys come four decisions: how long to let for, what rent to ask, how far to furnish, and who will manage tenants. Sean's checklist for new landlords.

qa.context: New investors often struggle after handover: finding and filtering tenants, setting rent and managing turnovers, while the instalment keeps coming every month and the unit sits empty.
qa.question: What should a new owner decide before letting out a unit?
qa.quote: there's no such thing as passive income
qa.answer: Settle four things: the tenancy length, the rent the market will bear, how much to furnish, and who will market and manage the unit. Spend a little to stand out, because a new project hands over hundreds of units at once, all chasing the same tenants.

reasons.title: Short or long stays
reasons.body: Short stays usually earn more, but checking guests in and out and cleaning between them is like running a hotel. Long tenancies can be set as 2+1, two years at a fixed rent with an option for one more.

reasons.title: The market sets the rent
reasons.body: Find out what similar units actually rent for from agents and the property portals before deciding what to ask.

reasons.title: Furnish to stand out
reasons.body: Letting a bare unit cheaply or furnishing well both have a cost. The aim is the minimum spend that makes tenants consider your unit first.

reasons.title: Someone has to manage it
reasons.body: Between tenants, someone must clean, inspect and check that utility bills are paid. Agents handle long lets; short-stay operators can run a unit for a share of the profit.

actions: Decide on short stays or a long tenancy, and the length, such as 2+1.
Check the going rent for similar units before you list.
Furnish just enough to rank among the first units tenants consider.
Choose who lists and manages the unit: yourself, an agent or an operator.
Arrange cleaning and a utilities check for each change of tenant.
qa.caveat: Short-stay letting may be restricted by your building's rules or local regulations; check before choosing it.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's English captions for this January 2018 vlog, his first sponsored video, made with a company that lets units to corporate clients and filmed in one of its units. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased.
